Tämä ei siis vielä ole hankintailmoitus tai tarjouspyyntö. Hankinnan kohteena on kuvantava virtausmikroskopiajärjestelmä (flow imaging microscopy) vedessä olevien partikkeleiden (kokojakauma 2µm – 1 mm) morfologiseen analysointiin ja lukumäärien arviointiin laboratorio-olosuhteissa. Laitteen tulee pystyä kuvantamaan planktonia ja muita vedessä olevia partikkeleita värikuvina, laskemaan kuvista solujen ja partikkeleiden kokoon, pigmentaatioon, väriin ja muotoon liittyviä indikaattoreita ja mahdollistamaan suurten näytemäärien käsittely helposti kohtuullisessa ajassa. Laitteen tulee pystyä erottelemaan kasviplanktonsolut muista partikkeleista klorofyllin fluoresenssin avulla ja mahdollistamaan fluoresoivien merkkiaineiden (FITC) käytön. Laitteen suorittamaa analytiikkaa pitää pystyä seuraamaan reaaliaikaisesti, laadunvalvonnan varmistamiseksi. Laitteen ohjelmiston pitää tukea partikkelidatan perusanalytiikkaa ja luokittelua. Laitetta pitää pystyä myös käyttämään luotettavasti kenttäolosuhteissa tutkimusaluksella. The object of the procurement is a flow imaging microscopy system for morphological analysis and numerical estimation of particles in water (size distribution 2µm – 1 mm) under laboratory conditions. The device must be able to image plankton and other particles in water as color images, calculate indicators related to cell and particle size, pigmentation, color and shape from the images, and enable the easy processing of large sample volumes in a reasonable time. The device must be able to separate phytoplankton cells from other particles using chlorophyll fluorescence and enable the use of fluorescent dyes (FITC). The analytics performed by the device must be able to be monitored in real time to ensure quality control. The device software must support basic analytics and classification of particle data. The device must also be able to be used reliably in field conditions on a research vessel. Minimum requirements / Minimivaatimukset - flow imaging microscopy for aquatic applications for particle size range 2µm – 1 mm - objective lenses to change microscopic magnification (with at least four different magnification levels from 2x to 20x), to allow optimal imaging of different size-classes. - fused silica flow cells, ranging from 50µm depth x 350 µm width to 1000 µm depth x 3000µm width - syringe pumps for fluidics, sample flow rate adjustable and at least at the range 0.1 – 10 mL / min - high-resolution camera (24 bit color TIFF), with a frame rate up to 100 frames per second - automated camera focus - possibility to trigger imaging based on fluorescence signal - a laser, 488 or 532 nm, with 40 mW output - two PMT-based fluorescence detectors; one for chlorophyll a (e.g. emission at >650 nm) and the other one at green (e.g. at 525 nm for 488 nm laser) or orange (e.g. at 575 nm for 532 nm laser). - Imbedded computer, and external monitor, wireless keyboard, mouse and USB dongle for software if needed - a satellite version of software for offline analysis - software for acquiring particle flowcytometric and image data, to display collected data in real time and to postprocess particle data (e.g., sort, filter, group, classify images based on their morphological parameters). - software must allow, for each particle, unique measurements based on shape and morphology must include diameter (spherical and area-based), length, width, aspect ratio, area, volume, circularity, elongation, compactness, circle fit, perimeter, convex perimeter, edge gradient, fiber curl.
